item.title: Opinion | Kids with no safe place to rest at night are becoming chronically homeless adults
item.description: Only 3% of the state’s homeless beds are reserved for youth, which feeds a pipeline to chronic homelessness. Most vulnerable: foster kids.

item.title: Scott Wiener passed laws that made it easier to build in California. Can he do the same in Congress?
item.description: If elected, will the prolific Wiener get housing laws passed at a national level? Or will Congress' tendency to inaction win out?

item.title: FPPC investigates ex-Newsom chief of staff
item.description: The FPPC is investigating Williamson after helping settle a lawsuit between the state and her former client, Activision Blizzard.

item.title: Opinion | Don’t clear the field in governor’s race by clearing out diversity
item.description: Most candidates urged to stay are white and backed by big money, but those urged to bow out are leaders of color with decades of public service. It's an issue in this state of diverse voters.

item.title: California sues Trump to keep shut oil pipeline on Santa Barbara coast
item.description: The state argues the Trump administration invented an energy emergency to justify forcing the restart of a shuttered offshore oil operation — setting a dangerous precedent for federal power over state law.

item.title: Opinion | Government money made Silicon Valley’s tech titans rich. A billionaire tax won't hurt them
item.description: The public helped create tech fortunes via government grants, defense contracts and corporate-friendly regulation. Some payback is in order.

item.title: Does lobbying at the Capitol work? These UC students say yes, and they’ve got receipts
item.description: University students lobbied at the California Capitol recently, backing bills to increase CalFresh eligibility, student housing and voting student regents.

item.title: Opinion | Medi-Cal faces funding emergency from state miscalculations, federal budget cuts
item.description: Gov. Gavin Newsom is retracting Medi-Cal for immigrants, years after he wrongly figured a state surplus. And President Trump is cutting health funds to states.

item.title: Digital tablets mellowed California prisons. Now a tech migration is riling users
item.description: Every incarcerated person in a California prison has a digital table enabling communication with the outside world. The system is changing vendors to lower costs.

item.title: Last-minute voter? The Supreme Court is coming for you
item.description: Justices could set a precedent in a decision about Mississippi ballots postmarked on Election Day but arriving after.
